_comment: B4: sharding. DroNet's own single-core latency is 113.7 ms against a 33.3 ms period, so it misses every deadline under EVERY placement policy, static pinning included -- no scheduler can fix a task whose service time exceeds its period. The only lever left is to spend more cores on one dispatch. Measured on the board, DroNet's total falls 113.7 -> 62.0 -> 32.4 ms on 1/2/4 cores, so a 4-core shard is the first configuration in which it can meet its deadline at all.
_capabilities_comment: IME is measured, not assumed: smt.vmadot executes on cores 0-3 and SIGILLs on 4-7 (artifacts/k1_bringup/*/ime_capability_probe.txt). It is therefore a property of cluster-0 cores, never a separate machine -- see xpu-rt/capabilities.py.
_concurrency_comment: machine_combination_mode=singletons: each of the 8 cores is independently schedulable, so 8 dispatches can genuinely run at once. This is why the profiles above are single-core (topo_0).
_shard_comment: machine_combination_mode=shard emits singletons PLUS aligned power-of-two core blocks, so the scheduler CHOOSES between running a dispatch on one core and spreading it across several. A block and the cores inside it intersect, so combinations_overlap serialises them and a 4-core shard excludes anything else on those cores -- the physical truth, enforced by the same set intersection that already prevents double-booking.
_topo_comment: topo_tag_override is FALSE here, unlike the singleton configs. With it true every combination is costed with topo_0, so a 4-core shard would be charged the SINGLE-core time while blocking four cores, and the solver would correctly never choose one -- reporting 'sharding does not help' for a purely clerical reason. Each block must be costed with its own N-hart profile, which the combination's topo tag already selects.
_instances_comment: Instance counts are pinned, not derived. The heuristic sizes the horizon from the profiles, so a faster configuration produces FEWER releases -- B4 came out at 7 mlp / 3 dronet against B1's 32 / 10, which would have compared two different workloads and flattered the faster one. 32 and 10 are one hyperperiod of {10, 33.3} ms and match every other rung.
